# 4 Gods + 4 Tauren

This is a stampede-control comp that wins by never letting the enemy act. Four Centaur pieces turn every melee step into a charging stun, Magnus pulls clumps together, and the three Tauren summon totems that taunt, silence and disarm. On top of that, Omniknight ("only knight") loops Guardian Angel every few seconds thanks to the God cooldown reduction, so the whole board sits under permanent damage reduction while Leshrac cooks everything with AoE magic. The recent patch dropped the Tauren costs, so Earthshaker and Elder Titan are now reliable to find, which is what made the comp consistent enough to climb with.

The power spike lands once you hit level 9-10 and fields both wizards, four Gods and the stampede package. Before that you're playing a normal tempo game — streak, bank gold, and stay flexible.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
|------|------|-----------|------|
| Leshrac | 5 | God, Druid, Centaur | Main carry — AoE magic nuke, wants all mana/spell items |
| Elder Titan | 4 | God, Druid, Tauren | Bridges Gods + Taurens; pairs with Leshrac for the Druid two-star trick |
| Spirit Breaker | 1 | Assassin, Tauren | Cheapest Tauren, front-line stun body |
| Earthshaker | 3 | Shaman, Tauren | The 3-cost Tauren the patch made findable |
| Magnus | 4 | Assassin, Centaur | AoE stun engine with Minotaur Horn |
| Centaur Warrunner | 2 | Centaur, Warrior | Fourth Centaur to unlock the level-4 stampede |
| Enchantress | 1 | Beast, Centaur, Druid | Extra Centaur + Druid, easy to three-star |
| Omniknight | 5 | Human, Knight | "Only knight" — Guardian Angel damage reduction on a short cooldown |
| Queen of Pain | 5 | Assassin, Demon | Secondary carry, pure damage + AoE control |
| Rubick | 3 | God, Wizard | Core God and one of your two wizards |
| Zeus | 5 | God, Mage | Rounds out the fourth God with burst + max-HP damage |

The Druid pairing between Leshrac and Elder Titan lets you drop an Io to instantly upgrade one of them — if one is already two-star, the Io forces the other to two-star.

## Items

Everything on the carry side is about mana and magic:

- **Leshrac** wants stacked mana generation so he casts non-stop: Refresher Orb (tier 4), Kaya (tier 2), Linkens Sphere (tier 3). At three-star his ultimate deletes packs.
- **Magnus** takes Minotaur Horn (tier 4) so he charges in and immediately AoE-stuns at the opening of the fight; Bottle (tier 2) gives him a near-instant first cast.
- **Queen of Pain** takes Dagon (tier 4) and Bloodthorn (tier 4) — instant damage that also feeds her mana. If a Divine Rapier (tier 5) floats to you late and you're about to die, she's the unit to put it on.
- **Omniknight** just needs to survive to cast, so Guardian Angel greaves-style defense like Guardian Greaves (tier 4) is enough.

Early on, grab any mana-regen scraps for the casters and armor for the front — nothing needs to be optimal before you stabilize.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

- **Early (rounds 1-10):** Commit to a streak, win or lose — either is fine, the point is stable gold. A two-star Shadow Demon is a fine reason to start winning.
- **Mid (rounds 10-20):** Bank economy and push to level 7 with purple units. Collect Druids for the Leshrac/Elder Titan pairing. Grab a strong relic — economy relics if you're streaking, damage-reduction relics if you're bleeding.
- **Level 9 (round ~21):** This is the real roll window. You want the better legendary/purple rates. Ban to improve hit chance — banning dwarves is cheap (about 4 gold) versus banning elves.
- **Level 10-11 (rounds 31+):** Roll for two-stars and any three-star Druid. Wait until after round 31 to roll hard, since lobbies get aggressive and you don't want to over-commit gold early.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Split your stampede units (Magnus, Spirit Breaker) to opposite corners so they charge across the board and stun the widest path. Keep Leshrac tucked in a back corner behind the chargers. Cluster your melee around Omniknight so everyone catches the Guardian Angel buff before diving.

The comp beats basically everything that relies on casting — the perma-stun and Tauren disarm/silence shut down alchemist summoners, mages and other control comps. Its clean answer is the Faceless (Void) comp, which is immune to your stuns and debuffs; against that you lean on Leshrac and Queen of Pain doing raw magic and pure damage rather than relying on control.
